findings.detail: Delete the last submodule and its checkout, then capture a committed or staged deletion with diff.ignoreSubmodules=all. Neither current index contains that gitlink, so submodules is empty. The scope collector includes the deletion using an explicit ignore override, but the rendered reviewer command omits that override and hides the deletion. Apply the override independently of current submodule presence.
findings.evidence: Both review-scope copies collect submodule records from the current real and temporary indexes at lines 312–316 and override ignore settings for bucket collection at lines 489–494. render_scope adds --ignore-submodules=none only when submodules is nonempty. Installed git-config documentation identifies diff.ignoreSubmodules as the default for git diff; git-diff documentation states that all hides every submodule change.
findings.title: Parallel paths: deleted submodules lose the rendered diff ignore override

findings.detail: A retained checkout staged for deletion, or an untracked embedded repository, produces an aggregate untracked entry such as module/. Bucket extension preserves that entry alongside recursive internal paths. codex-aspects rejects every path containing an empty segment, including a trailing slash, so prompt, changes and gate reject the newly supported scope as invalid. Handle these directory entries consistently across collection and consumption.
findings.evidence: review-scope:495 collects untracked entries directly from git ls-files; extend_submodule_buckets:349–350 retains them unchanged. codex-aspects:204–207 rejects trailing slashes, and require_scope_file:265 applies that rule to untracked. A read-only Git probe using the existing external checkout's index and the reviewed repository's parent as --work-tree returned exactly 523-review-snapshot-submodules/. The deleted fixture exercises collection but never passes its resulting scope through an aspect consumer. Both canonical collectors have identical behavior.
findings.title: Parallel paths: retained checkout scopes fail the aspect consumer's path validation

findings.detail: This paragraph predates the change. It says staging or unstaging an already tracked path leaves snapshot unchanged and that the index counts only when tracking membership changes. The helper hashes semantic index content and bucket membership, including recursively captured child indexes, so ordinary staging can move snapshot while tree stays unchanged. The main skill and snapshot reference describe the implemented behavior correctly.
findings.evidence: reviewers.md:131 claims staging and unstaging leave the snapshot unchanged. review-scope:564–573 hashes the index digest and all four buckets. scope-and-snapshot.md explicitly states that staging, unstaging and intent-to-add move snapshot even when tree stays unchanged; the main review-until-clean skill states the same at line 58.
findings.title: Docs drift: edit-round explanation still describes snapshots as insensitive to staging
